title: A nanogram-sensitive workflow for oligonucleotide mass spectrometry using ion-pair-free nanoflow HILIC and RNase benchmarking.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed all 32 files in PRIDE project PXD070755 via the PRIDE API: 14 Thermo .raw files (282-926 MB each, about 8 GB total) and 18 small mzTab search-result files (2-232 KB). Downloaded the largest mzTab (NIST_mRNA_T1_250ng_1.mzTab): 851 oligonucleotide-spectrum-match rows with sequence, modifications, retention time, charge, observed and calculated m/z, and NASE (NucleicAcidSearchEngine) scores.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the samples are yeast tRNAPhe, tRNAIle, an HDV-ribozyme construct with/without pseudouridine, and NIST firefly luciferase mRNA digested by RNase T1, RNase 4 and colicin E5. Supplementary tables were not retrievable (Europe PMC supplement endpoint timed out).

a1_downloadable.note: PRIDE PXD070755 is public; file listing and one mzTab downloaded without login (checked).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No ML target exists as a designed column. The only candidate label is retention time per identified oligonucleotide in the mzTab files, a by-product of a methods benchmark, not a curated outcome table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Oligonucleotide sequences and modifications are present as text in the mzTab rows (checked one file).

a4_units_stated.note: mzTab is a standard format with retention time in seconds and m/z defined by the spec (checked header).

a5_enough_rows.note: Largest mzTab has 851 matches; 18 files total likely a few thousand rows, but they are repeated spectra of fragments from only ~4 RNA molecules, so unique sequences are probably in the low hundreds. Total not counted.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <5 MB for mzTabs; ~8 GB if raw spectra were needed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Search results are tiny; raw spectra (needed for any spectrum-level task) exceed the 50 MB cap and the 5 GB working-set guideline.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not cross-checked against paper identification counts; file names match the sample design described in the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The identifications themselves are outputs of NASE database search (a scoring model), and retention times come from one HILIC setup; any sequence label would be distilling the search engine.

existing_models.name: Gradient boosting / SVR retention-time models for ion-pair oligonucleotide chromatography (J Chromatogr A 2022, PubMed 40014960)
ML retention-time prediction on larger antisense oligonucleotide datasets (arXiv 2511.15753)
Kinetic CID spectrum prediction for deprotonated oligonucleotides (JASMS 2025)

backbone.name: RNA-FM (RNA language model) in principle, but oligos are 3-20 nt with modifications

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None worth stating; the dataset covers too few molecules to add to MODOMICS-scale knowledge.

controls.positive_control: Retention time should rise with oligonucleotide length (stated in HILIC literature).
controls.external_validation: None identified for nanoflow HILIC of RNase digests.

honest_claim_h3: Could only claim to predict HILIC retention of RNase fragments from four RNA molecules on one instrument setup in one lab.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use short RNA fragment sequences and modifications to predict when they come off a chromatography column.
plain_idea.train_on: Sequence and modifications of each identified RNA fragment from mass-spectrometry search results; unknown number of unique fragments, likely a few hundred.
plain_idea.predict: Retention time on the authors' nanoflow HILIC (hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography) column, as recorded by the instrument for search-engine-identified fragments.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Better retention prediction could help RNA mass-spec search engines reject false matches, but this dataset is too narrow to train a general model.

label_elsewhere.sources: Oligonucleotide retention-time datasets exist for ion-pair reversed-phase chromatography of antisense oligos (found by search), not for HILIC of RNase digests.
label_elsewhere.why: Different chromatography modes make cross-dataset training largely incompatible.

ml_idea: HILIC retention-time prediction for RNase-digested RNA oligonucleotides from mzTab identifications; rejected because few unique sequences, labels derived from search-engine output, and no designed outcome table.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 18 mzTab file sizes (total under 1 MB); nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Concatenate all 18 mzTabs and count unique (sequence, modification) pairs at 1% FDR; under ~400 kills it.

verdict_reason: Methods paper with ~8 GB raw spectra and 18 small search-result files covering about four RNA molecules; no designed label column, too few unique items, and identifications are search-engine outputs (A2, A5, A8 fail).
